headline: GridRush: Make Words, Then Build a Sentence
problemStatement: A vocabulary race is more useful when learners can see the letters, test a word, and then reuse their discoveries in meaningful writing. GridRush has two timed rounds: students make words from a shared letter grid, then create a sentence using words they found.
outcomes: Retrieve and spell vocabulary using a common set of letters.
Notice topic words and bonus-letter words while building a class word wall.
Transfer collected words into a grammatical sentence.
howItWorks: The teacher starts a round with a 3-by-3 letter grid. Students see the same grid on their phones and can tap letters or type a word.
Letters may be reused. Each submitted word receives checking feedback on the phone, including points when accepted or the reason it was crossed out when rejected.
The live word wall highlights topic and bonus-letter words, grows longer words visually, and tracks counts for each student.
In Round 2, each student writes one sentence using at least two of their Round 1 words. Sentence results remain stable on phones while learners type.
teacherUseCases: Use Round 1 to activate vocabulary before a writing task, then keep Round 2 as a short transfer exercise.
Discuss the longest word or a topic word from the live wall and ask students to use it in another sentence.

faq.q: Can letters be reused in a word?
faq.a: Yes. A letter can be used more than once as students make words from the 3-by-3 grid, as long as every letter appears somewhere in that grid.

faq.q: What happens when a word is rejected?
faq.a: The phone shows checking feedback and the reason a word was crossed out. Rejected words score zero, so a short invalid entry does not earn points.

faq.q: What is the second round for?
faq.a: Students write one sentence using two or more words they collected in Round 1. The game keeps those results attached to each phone while the sentence is being written.

faq.q: Does the teacher see every student's word?
faq.a: The teacher sees the class word wall and student counts during the race. Topic words and bonus-letter words are highlighted to support a quick class review.
